method: Read-only reading of build-trace/main generated C (allocating functions, their callers, exported getters that load the same globals/offsets), RTTI/exports of dump/exefs/main via research/tools/rtti.py. No game run. 'certain' only where an exported getter returns the field by a plain load; constructor/reader evidence is 'probable'. App classes here have no RTTI, so class names come from the exported functions that reach the same global.

sites.what: lib::EffectManager (visual effects manager): 128 effect slots of 0x300 bytes (0x18000) followed by ~6 KB of manager tables. Reader f_7100561b60 is the effect manager's per-frame update (same code unit as the allocator).

fields.meaning: effect slot i (i = top byte of an effect handle)
full effect handle stored in the slot (generation | index<<24); a handle is alive when it equals this word
effect position (written by set_pos when slot+0x2D6 is set)
alternative/pending position used when slot+0x2D6 is clear; slot+0x2DA set to 1 as a dirty flag
per-slot scale/colour factors initialised to 1.0

sites.evidence: Allocator f_710055d080 (boot): allocates 0x19890 bytes, zeroes 0x18000, loops 128 x 0x300 initialising slots, then stores the block into a 16-byte holder whose address goes to 0x7105334920 = exported EffectManager singleton. Exported is_exist/set_pos index the block by (handle>>24)*0x300 and check slot+4. Presentation (visual effects); the simulation only holds handles to it (EffectModule) and may ask is_exist, so it is not a simulation owner of state.

sites.what: app::FighterEntry: one per player entry (index 0..7), owned by app::FighterManager. Holds the entry's FighterInformation (stocks, rebirth, counters), the list of the entry's Fighter objects (several for Ice Climbers/Pokemon Trainer), the current fighter index, per-fighter AI objects. Caller 0x71014ec2bc (match load); reader f_710157d6f0 per frame.
sites.owner_global: 0x71052b94f8 (export lib::Singleton<app::FighterManager>::instance_) -> FighterManager -> [0] data -> +0x20 + 8*entry_id; entry count at data+0xA0

fields.meaning: number of fighters in the entry
entry id (FighterEntryID) written by the constructor
the entry's FighterInformation interface
stock count (FighterInformation data +0xD8)
is on rebirth (respawn platform) (FighterInformation data +0x38C)

fields.type: u64 count, Fighter*[] inline vector, u8
fields.meaning: number of Fighter objects, the Fighter pointers, current fighter index (current_fighter_id reads fighters[entry+0x5918])

sites.evidence: Allocator f_7100678150(manager_data, entry_id, ...) allocates 0x5AC0, sets embedded vptrs at +0xF0/+0x100 (data pointer = entry+0x110), +0x4140 small-vector header (+0x4148 capacity 3, +0x4150 count 0, +0x4158 -> +0x4160), stores the block at manager_data+0x20+8*id and increments manager_data+0xA0. The exported FighterManager__get_fighter_entry_impl reads exactly manager->[0]+0x20+8*id. Stocks, rebirth state and the per-entry fighter list are per-match game state.

Reader f_7100327650(block, fighter_index) updates one record per frame after asking the AI manager for that fighter's status flags.

sites.evidence: Allocated in f_7100309030 (AI manager setup, called at 0x71014de0c4 with x0 = *(*0x71052b6fd8)); block pointer stored in a holder written to manager+0xB0. Exports app::ai::target_id/check_target_stat_* use the same manager (lookup -> +0x54 flags); ai_stage::current_id returns manager+0x150 by a plain load, ai_camera::dead_* read manager+0xC8, ai_dangerzone::* manager+0xC0. Drives CPU decisions, so it is simulation state whenever CPU players fight (the CPU-vs-CPU runs).

Reader f_7100368210 = app::ai::get_cmd_id_from_req_id_with_predict (CPU command choice), which reaches it through the AI Lua state's extra space (lua_State - 8).

sites.evidence: f_71006b6f10 constructs the 0x80-byte object (base vptr 0x7104F6BCE0, final 0x7104F85D30), stores the player index (<8) at +0x8, a kind read from 0x71052C50F0 table at +0x50, then allocates 0xCD0. Its caller loops over the entry's fighters (count at entry+0x28) and stores each object in an array. The app::ai exports read (lua_State-8)+0xC50, consistent with a context of this size. CPU decision state: simulation state for CPU players (probable link to lua_State).

sites.evidence: Allocated in the match-setup function f_7101344cf0 (0x11B0 bytes, embedded vptrs 0x7104F76088/0x7104F76038), block stored in a holder written to 0x71052b8f00. app::camera::get_dead_area / get_camera_limit_range / target_pos load those offsets from *(*0x71052b8f00). outside_blocks.what: Not jemalloc: f_71039635c0 is the nus3 audio engine's update, run on the thread named 'nus3::audio update' (entry f_7103987e40, which calls f_71039635c0). Its state sits in main's own .bss (0x7106DD5000.., about 0x900 bytes of engine statics behind a std::recursive_mutex) plus memory the audio engine sub-allocates itself (its allocator wrapper at 0x710373e524, e.g. the 131,112-byte block it reads) and that thread's static 128 KB stack in .bss at 0x7106DD6000. The ~27 KB outside traced blocks is most likely that audio memory plus guest stacks: sound, not simulation.
outside_blocks.evidence: f_710373e630 (nus3 audio init) creates a thread: thread object 0x7106DD5CC0, entry 0x7103987E40, stack 0x7106DD6000 with size 0x20000, then names it with the rodata string 'nus3::audio update' (0x710435A148); it also references 'nuscFileAsyncRequest'. f_7103987e40 calls f_71039635c0 (its only caller). f_71039635c0 makes 163 references to 0x7106DD5xxx (main .bss: bss runs to 0x7107447100) and calls the imported std::__1::recursive_mutex::lock/unlock (GOT 0x710529FC00/08). jemalloc itself is 0x7103900000-0x7103960000 (aligned_alloc 0x710392e290, free 0x710392eb40); 0x71039635c0 lies just past it, which explains the 'near jemalloc' label. Which bytes make up the 27 KB was not checked against a trace.
